One thing I'll mention, I think the passion flower is one of the coolest looking things around. But I've witnessed every spring since I've planted them that they want to spread out, popping up new plants all around the original. I'm glad it's in the yard so I can just mow around it to keep it contained. In another location it might be a headache.
Passion fruit is a very aggressive vine. It can choke out large trees if left to it's own devices. Chop it down with impunity after every growing season if need be.

Now comes the wait - you will need to wait a long time for the fruit to turn completely purple, almost black. When it is ready, the fruit will drop off the vine - that's the best time to cut it open and scoop out the pulp and seeds. Don't pick it when it is still green or light purple.
